data.title: Canadian Stock Market Today: TSX Futures Edge Lower On Energy Inflation And Retail Focus
data.description:
The Morning Bull - Canadian Market Morning Update Friday, 23 Oct 2026

Canadian equities look set for a cautious open, with sentiment dominated by a fresh inflation shock from the commodity complex rather than offshore data. Investors are treating the move as a warning on domestic price pressure.

Canada’s Raw Materials Price Index jumped 4.8% in September, powered by a 14.4% surge in crude energy products. Producer prices rose 2.0% over the month. Together, these releases flag a stronger pipeline of costs feeding into future inflation gauges.

Higher input prices often feed into borrowing costs as rate expectations adjust. That can squeeze margins for manufacturers and other cost heavy businesses if they struggle to pass on higher energy and materials costs, especially with new home prices slipping 0.2%.

The immediate question is whether upcoming Canadian retail sales later today confirm resilient demand or show consumers already under strain. That single data point could either reinforce the inflation risk narrative or give investors more confidence that pricing pressure may be absorbed.

Stocks to Watch Before the Opening Bell

Thomson Reuters (TRI)

Thomson Reuters just rolled out CoCounsel Tax, Audit & Accounting, a next generation AI platform aimed at professional users. The tool is built to anchor every calculation in the relevant rule book and show how each answer is produced. Watch how quickly large firms adopt it and whether management starts tying the product to revenue or subscription metrics.

Mullen Group (MTL)

Mullen Group reported record quarterly revenue and operating income before depreciation and amortization across all segments for the period to September 30, 2026. Management points to internal expansion, acquisitions, and higher fuel surcharges as key drivers. Pay attention to how future updates describe demand tied to Nation Building Projects and any further acquisition activity.

Alimentation Couche-Tard (ATD)

Alimentation Couche-Tard agreed to buy retail assets from Irving Oil in Quebec and Ontario. The deal adds more stores and fuel outlets to the network, which puts attention on future volume trends and fuel margins. Investors will be watching the next results or transaction update for detail on integration costs and any early contribution from the acquired locations.

Top Movers

  • FirstService (TSX:FSV) jumped 7.41% after Q3 results showed 6% revenue growth and management reaffirmed full year confidence.
  • Constellation Software (TSX:CSU) gained 5.33% as investors responded to the appointment of a new Chief AI Officer.
  • WSP Global (TSX:WSP) rose 4.94% following fresh attention on environmental services revenue and commentary highlighting the stock as undervalued.

Top Losers

  • Celestica (TSX:CLS) fell 12.04% as investors reacted to concerns about funding availability for future AI infrastructure spending.
  • Hemlo Mining (TSX:HMMC) declined 11.42% after fresh Q3 operating data highlighted production challenges linked to an electrical substation outage.
  • Americas Gold and Silver (TSX:USA) fell 11.29% following recent production figures and ahead of the next quarterly earnings release in November.

On The Radar

Canadian trading over the next few sessions revolves around retail demand, central bank decisions, and a heavy slate of Q3 earnings from energy, materials, and transport stocks.

  • Canada Retail Sales MoM Final, Fri 23 Oct. August sales carry a consensus call of 1.3% after a 0.7% decline, so a weaker print would underline household strain and ease pressure on rate expectations after this week’s materials-led inflation surprise.
  • Canada Retail Sales Ex Autos MoM, Fri 23 Oct. The core August figure is forecast at 0.9% after a 0.7% drop, and anything well below that would point to softer discretionary spending and could weigh on Canadian bank and consumer-linked stocks.
  • Bank of Canada Interest Rate Decision, Wed 28 Oct. Markets are looking for a move to 2.5% from 2.25%, so any different outcome or tone in the Monetary Policy Report would directly affect borrowing costs, rate-sensitive equities, and the Canadian dollar.
  • Kinross Gold, Wed 28 Oct. Q3 results after the close will put the focus on cash costs and margins from its gold operations, which matter for how investors treat the wider Canadian precious metals group after recent production headlines elsewhere.
  • Teck Resources, Thu 29 Oct. Pre-market Q3 numbers will shine a light on realized prices and unit costs in its coal and base metals businesses, key for sentiment across Canadian miners that are highly exposed to global commodity demand.

Sector & Industry Watch

Energy: Oil strength offsets cost squeeze

Energy has inched higher over the past week, with Oil and Gas tracking that move as firmer crude prices show up in sector returns. The jump in Canada’s raw materials inflation that came mostly from energy improves revenue potential for producers while also lifting fuel surcharges for transport groups such as Mullen Group.

The key swing factor now is how early November Q3 reports from large Canadian Oil and Gas stocks talk about spending plans and payouts against this higher price and cost backdrop.

Materials: Miners struggle with hot input prices

Materials have retreated sharply over the last seven days, with Metals and Mining sliding even more as the sector works through weaker recent performance. The latest producer price and raw material inflation data show energy and input costs running hot, which can pressure budgets for gold, copper, lithium, and potash projects tied to companies such as Imperial Metals and E3 Lithium.

The next checkpoint is the coming wave of Q3 production and earnings releases flagged across Canadian miners like Fortuna Mining and Discovery Mining, since any change in cost guidance or development timelines can quickly move this slice of a diversified portfolio.

Real Estate: Rate relief meets softer housing data

Real Estate has bounced over the past week, although 1 year returns remain weaker than the broader Canadian Market. Higher borrowing costs still weigh on REITs and developers, because more interest expense leaves less room for distributions and new projects, and that now lines up with September data showing new home prices slipping 0.2% and land values declining 0.9%.

For property linked holdings, focus falls on how listed vehicles such as RioCan, Canadian Apartment Properties REIT, and FirstService describe occupancy, rents, and refinancing when they next update investors, since those details tie directly into income stability.

Financials: Banks balance rate income and consumer strain

Financials have edged higher over the last seven days, with Banks still showing firm 1 year gains after recent results from Toronto Dominion Bank highlighted strong earnings in core Canadian operations. Higher rates support loan and deposit income for firms such as TD, RBC, Manulife, and Sun Life, although steeper mortgage and card payments can eventually pressure household budgets.

The main domestic data point for this group is today’s Canadian retail sales report, which gives a clearer read on how consumer spending, credit card volumes, and small business receipts are holding up against higher borrowing costs.

Tech: AI headlines contrast with weak chip trend

Tech has slipped over the past week, while Semiconductors have fallen much more over the same period and over the year to date. Company news still points to demand for AI and software, from Thomson Reuters rolling out its CoCounsel platform to SalesCloser’s patent filing on multi agent call technology and TD’s Credit Assist tool in commercial banking.

The catalyst that matters most now is the upcoming Canadian Tech earnings season, where commentary on IT and AI budgets from software and platform providers will show whether current share price pressure lines up with business conditions or has run ahead of them.

data.title: Netflix, Inc. Beat Analyst Estimates: See What The Consensus Is Forecasting For Next Year
data.description:
Netflix, Inc. (NASDAQ:NFLX) shareholders are probably feeling a little disappointed, since its shares fell 7.7% to US$67.05 in the week after its latest quarterly results. Netflix reported US$13b in revenue, roughly in line with analyst forecasts, although statutory earnings per share (EPS) of US$0.87 beat expectations, being 5.8% higher than what the analysts expected. Following the result, the analysts have updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. So we gathered the latest post-earnings forecasts to see what estimates suggest is in store for next year.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Following the latest results, Netflix's 45 analysts are now forecasting revenues of US$56.6b in 2027. This would be a solid 14% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Per-share earnings are expected to increase 6.2% to US$3.77. Yet prior to the latest earnings, the analysts had been anticipated revenues of US$57.0b and earnings per share (EPS) of US$3.80 in 2027. So it's pretty clear that, although the analysts have updated their estimates, there's been no major change in expectations for the business following the latest results.

View our latest analysis for Netflix

The consensus price target fell 7.9% to US$84.83, suggesting that the analysts might have been a bit enthusiastic in their previous valuation - or they were expecting the company to provide stronger guidance in the quarterly results. Fixating on a single price target can be unwise though, since the consensus target is effectively the average of analyst price targets. As a result, some investors like to look at the range of estimates to see if there are any diverging opinions on the company's valuation. There are some variant perceptions on Netflix, with the most bullish analyst valuing it at US$126 and the most bearish at US$57.00 per share. This is a fairly broad spread of estimates, suggesting that analysts are forecasting a wide range of possible outcomes for the business.

One way to get more context on these forecasts is to look at how they compare to both past performance, and how other companies in the same industry are performing. The period to the end of 2027 brings more of the same, according to the analysts, with revenue forecast to display 11% growth on an annualised basis. That is in line with its 11% annual growth over the past five years. Compare this with the broader industry, which analyst estimates (in aggregate) suggest will see revenues grow 8.6% annually. So although Netflix is expected to maintain its revenue growth rate, it's definitely expected to grow faster than the wider industry.

The Bottom Line

The most important thing to take away is that there's been no major change in sentiment, with the analysts reconfirming that the business is performing in line with their previous earnings per share estimates. Fortunately, they also reconfirmed their revenue numbers, suggesting that it's tracking in line with expectations. Additionally, our data suggests that revenue is expected to grow faster than the wider industry. Furthermore, the analysts also cut their price targets, suggesting that the latest news has led to greater pessimism about the intrinsic value of the business.

With that in mind, we wouldn't be too quick to come to a conclusion on Netflix. Long-term earnings power is much more important than next year's profits. At Simply Wall St, we have a full range of analyst estimates for Netflix going out to 2028, and you can see them free on our platform here..

data.title: How Investors Are Reacting To bioMérieux (ENXTPA:BIM) Rapid Vaginitis Test Clearance
data.description:
• bioMérieux reported that its BIOFIRE SPOTFIRE Vaginitis Panel received both FDA 510(k) clearance and a CLIA waiver, enabling rapid multiplex PCR testing for eight vaginitis pathogens at the point of care using self collected or clinician collected swabs.
  • This first rapid molecular vaginitis test extends bioMérieux’s SPOTFIRE menu beyond respiratory and sore throat panels and is intended to deepen reagent usage on an existing modular installed base across family practices, urgent care clinics, and OB/GYN offices.
  • The next step is to examine how bioMérieux’s new CLIA waived, rapid vaginitis panel could reshape the investment narrative around SPOTFIRE utilization.

bioMérieux Investment Narrative Recap

For bioMérieux, the core belief is that BIOFIRE and SPOTFIRE reagent usage, industrial applications, and GO•28 efficiency gains can keep offsetting weaker instrument demand, softer respiratory testing and pressure in China. The new CLIA waived SPOTFIRE vaginitis panel fits cleanly into that story by adding another non respiratory assay that can run on an already large installed base.

The key near term swing factor is how consistently SPOTFIRE reagent volumes build, given prior concern around volatility in placements and expiring pandemic era contracts. The biggest risk remains a mix of weaker instruments, ongoing China softness and higher U.S. tariffs, and this new panel on its own does not remove those pressures.

The dual FDA 510(k) clearance and CLIA waiver for the BIOFIRE SPOTFIRE Vaginitis Panel looks most relevant because it speaks directly to syndromic growth and reagent intensity. A CLIA waiver allows non lab clinicians to run the test in family practices, urgent care and OB/GYN offices, which ties neatly into the push for broader point of care usage on SPOTFIRE.

For catalysts, the key question is whether more non respiratory cartridges like this can keep reagent growth closer to the roughly 40% SPOTFIRE reagent increase reported in the second quarter of 2026, even if instruments stay weaker. Execution risk sits in training non lab staff, managing turnaround times at scale, and making sure pricing still supports GO•28 margin ambitions in the face of higher U.S. tariffs and a slower China business.

How the SPOTFIRE Vaginitis Panel Fits Into bioMérieux’s Consensus Story

Analysts looking at bioMérieux are effectively asking whether products like the BIOFIRE SPOTFIRE Vaginitis Panel can support steady expansion in testing volume while headwinds in instruments and China continue. The consensus currently assumes revenue increases of 5.4% per year for the next three years, which implies a measured build rather than a sprint, with syndromic and point of care menus expected to carry more of the load.

Earnings expectations already bake in higher profitability. Forecasts point to earnings of €586.7 million by 2029, compared with €462.6 million today, which is an increase of about €124 million. That move is paired with an assumed margin shift from 11.6% to 12.5% over three years, so every extra test on SPOTFIRE, including the vaginitis panel, matters more to the bottom line than it would have a few years ago.

Valuation assumptions also lean on this earnings trajectory. On the numbers published, bioMérieux would need to reach €4.7b of revenue and €586.7 million of earnings in 2029 while trading on a P/E of 19.5x, compared with 22.2x today. The current analyst consensus price target of €79.9 sits about 9.2% below the recent share price of €87.25, which suggests the market is already giving the group credit for a fair portion of that execution.

For the SPOTFIRE Vaginitis Panel specifically, the CLIA waiver is what ties the clinical story to this financial framework. By allowing non lab clinicians in family medicine, urgent care and OB/GYN settings to run a multiplex vaginitis PCR, the test is designed to support exactly the kind of reagent intensity that underpins those margin and earnings expectations, without needing a comparable lift in instrument placements.

There is still tension between the upside and the risks. The same consensus that embeds growth from non respiratory testing also highlights double digit instrument declines in recent quarters, China revenue pressure in 2025 and early 2026, and higher U.S. tariffs adding €20 million to €24 million of extra cost this year. To see meaningful benefit from the new panel, usage has to scale fast enough and at pricing that offsets these known drags.

Investors watching bioMérieux may want to track a few concrete datapoints over the next couple of years. These include the mix of respiratory versus non respiratory SPOTFIRE cartridges, adoption of the vaginitis panel across primary care and OB/GYN clinics, how often clinicians use self collected versus clinician collected swabs in real practice, and whether training demands slow uptake. Each of those elements feeds back into the same question that runs through the analyst models: Can BIOFIRE and SPOTFIRE keep reagent growth and margins on the consensus path even if instruments and China stay under pressure?

bioMérieux’s current analyst narrative points to €4.7b in revenue and €586.7 million in earnings by 2029, based on revenue growing 5.4% per year and an earnings increase of about €124 million from €462.6 million today.
